clue.text: Growing attractive

definitions.meaning: ... as in coming to be, turning into something over time
... as in flattering, suiting the wearer well

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the participle of 'become' means coming to be, and the adjective means flattering or suitable.

clue.text: Duck casserole at last — man looked up

indicators.note: in a down clue, looked up means the word is read from bottom to top, so backwards
at last points to the final letter of the word casserole

parts.note: Dave is a man's name

explanation.surface: A diner glances up once the duck casserole is finally finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'looked up' turns the whole run E + DAVE, read upwards in this down entry; E is the last letter of 'casserole'.
explanation.definitionFit: To duck a question or blow is to dodge or sidestep it, a verb synonym.

clue.text: Unpaid superior

explanation.definitionFit: Two senses of one adjective: an unsettled bill remains owed, and exceptional quality stands out above the rest.

clue.text: Popular vote Peter failed to secure not clever

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast around, so the jumbled name wraps the vote
failed suggests the name Peter has gone wrong and is jumbled

parts.note: X is the cross marked on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: A candidate called Peter failed to win the popular vote and was thought foolish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failed' rearranges PETER as EPERT, and 'to secure' puts X inside it after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unskilled or lacking expertise is inexpert, a rough synonym for not clever.

clue.text: Attack a person's kid and make them angry?

parts.note: to get someone can mean to attack or get at them
someone's means belonging to a person
a kid is a young goat; here the word stands for the animal

explanation.surface: Someone assaults a neighbour's young goat, which naturally upsets its owner.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads literally, but the idiom means to irritate someone.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to annoy or irritate a person intensely, an everyday figurative expression.

clue.text: Excessively sentimental American going over Indiana port

indicators.note: going over suggests turning over, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: Gary is a port city on Lake Michigan in Indiana

explanation.surface: An American travels across to a harbour town in Indiana, getting sentimental.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going over' suggests travel, but it signals the abbreviation is turned round. Gary, Indiana, sits on Lake Michigan.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugary describes cloying sweetness, used figuratively of mawkish, sickly sentiment.

clue.text: Military band?

parts.note: not a group of soldiers playing music but a strip of braid on a uniform sleeve showing rank

explanation.definitionFit: A rank insignia sewn on a soldier's sleeve is a band of fabric, so a military band.

clue.text: Extremely gleeful about a female noted in Kalamazoo

indicators.note: about means going around, so the outer letters surround the next piece
extremely points to the extreme, outermost letters of gleeful

explanation.surface: A happy woman is celebrated in song in a Michigan town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremely' gives G and L, the first and last letters of 'gleeful'; 'about' puts them round A. The song 'I've Got a Gal in Kalamazoo' was a 1942 Glenn Miller hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Gal is informal for a girl or woman, and the famous song names one from Kalamazoo.

clue.text: Engineers succeeded without adapting Crusoe's means

indicators.note: without means outside, so the final letter stands beyond the rearranged name

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers of the British Army

indicators.note: adapting means altering, so the letters of the name are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
S is the abbreviation for succeeded in genealogies

explanation.surface: Army engineers succeed by adapting what Robinson Crusoe had available.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adapting' rearranges CRUSOE as SOURCE; 'without' places S outside it at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's means are their resources, the money and assets available to them.

clue.text: Trivial talk that led to Tweedledum and Tweedledee's quarrel?

definitions.text: that led to Tweedledum and Tweedledee's quarrel?
definitions.meaning: in Through the Looking-Glass the twins agree to fight because one has spoilt the other's nice new baby's toy

explanation.definitionFit: Rattle means to chatter on idly, and a baby's rattle is what the Lewis Carroll twins fought over.

clue.text: Permanently lively girl tours country and gets thrown out

indicators.note: tours means goes around, so the girl's name surrounds the rest

parts.note: Tess is a girl's name

indicators.note: gets thrown out tells us the word and is removed

parts.note: Ireland is a country
taken as written

explanation.surface: A girl tours a country, gets ejected, and keeps her energy throughout.
explanation.walkthrough: 'country' looks like the definition beside 'Permanently lively', but the definition is only the first two words; 'gets thrown out' removes a word of the clue itself, and 'tours' wraps the girl round what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Tireless means never flagging, always energetic, so lively without end.

clue.text: Attend course for law enforcement officers

definitions.meaning: read as two words, to ... somewhere is to attend it
a police officer's regular patrol route

explanation.definitionFit: Split as two words it means to be present, and whole it is a constable's patrol round.

clue.text: Doing well in the Duke of Milan's university

indicators.note: in places the university abbreviation inside the possessive name

parts.note: Prospero is the deposed Duke of Milan in Shakespeare's The Tempest

explanation.surface: Someone thriving at the university belonging to a Shakespearean duke.
explanation.walkthrough: U goes inside PROSPERO'S, before the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosperous means flourishing or successful, especially financially, so doing well.

clue.text: Butler, an idle 'un said to be coarse

parts.note: Rab Butler was a leading British Conservative politician of the mid-twentieth century

indicators.note: said tells us the phrase is spoken, giving the sound of the remaining letters

parts.note: an idle one is a lazy one, said casually as a lazy 'un

explanation.surface: A butler is called lazy and is judged crude.
explanation.walkthrough: RAB, a lazy 'un, spoken quickly, sounds like the answer. R. A. Butler, known as Rab, was a British Chancellor and Home Secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabelaisian describes earthy, bawdy humour like that of the French writer Rabelais, hence coarse.

clue.text: Nuts were put out in feeder

indicators.note: put out suggests disturbed or upset, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sets nuts out in a bird feeder.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a bird feeder; the feeder is a woman who suckles another's baby.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to breastfeed another woman's child is a feeder in the literal sense.

clue.text: Train in hospital department these days

parts.note: ENT is the ear, nose and throat department of a hospital
our age is the present time, these days

explanation.surface: A trainee works in a hospital department in modern times.
explanation.definitionFit: A train is a retinue of attendants following an important person, as is an entourage.

clue.text: Male kangaroo some Australians try to make fast

definitions.meaning: the male of several animals, including kangaroos
in Australian slang to have a go is to give it a ...
the idiom about earning money quickly and easily

explanation.definitionFit: The word names a male animal, is Australian slang for an attempt, and is the money in a quick-profit idiom.

clue.text: Strange planes or one's own?

indicators.note: strange suggests something odd or out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the aircraft are odd or belong to them.
explanation.definitionFit: Personal means belonging to a particular individual, private, so one's own.

clue.text: The Case of the Seamstress in the Tuileries

indicators.note: in signals the letters sit within the words the Tuileries

explanation.surface: A detective-story title about a dressmaker at the Paris gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: An etui is a small ornamental case for needles and sewing tools, as a seamstress would carry.

clue.text: Pointer starts to sniff scent? It's uncalled-for

parts.note: the needle of a dial or compass is its pointer

indicators.note: starts to points to the opening letters of the following words

explanation.surface: A pointer dog begins sniffing a scent, which seems unnecessary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pointer' looks like a gun dog; it is the needle on a gauge.
explanation.definitionFit: Needless means unnecessary or gratuitous, so uncalled-for, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Insincere talk about Guangzhou

parts.note: cant is hypocritical, sanctimonious talk
on means about, concerning

explanation.surface: Someone speaks hypocritically about a Chinese city.
explanation.definitionFit: Canton was the old European name for the southern Chinese city now called Guangzhou.

clue.text: Girls in Chinese dynasty assumed to protect pupils?

parts.note: the Sung (Song) dynasty ruled China from 960 to 1279
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Schoolgirls in ancient China are thought to shield their students.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pupils' are not schoolchildren but the centres of the eyes; shades are put on to protect them.
explanation.definitionFit: Dark glasses are put on, or assumed, to shield the eyes' pupils from bright light.

clue.text: One volunteers to carry love letter

indicators.note: to carry means to hold within, so the love symbol sits inside

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A volunteer agrees to deliver a love letter.
explanation.walkthrough: O goes inside ITA, between the I and the TA.
explanation.definitionFit: Iota is the ninth letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: Marks in the English essay

indicators.note: in places the abbreviation inside the next pieces

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: A teacher's marks appear in an English essay.
explanation.walkthrough: M goes between THE and E.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is a short school composition on a set subject, so an essay.

clue.text: Raised, voice in argument beside river

indicators.note: beside means next to, so the argument stands alongside the river

parts.note: the Fal is a river in Cornwall
a set-to is a fight or argument

explanation.surface: Voices are raised in an argument by the riverside.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma is surface punctuation; the definition is a raised voice.
explanation.definitionFit: Falsetto is the artificially high singing voice above a man's natural range.

clue.text: Determined to decline.

definitions.meaning: ... means resolved, as in ... on going
the sun is said to ... as it goes down

explanation.definitionFit: Set means firmly resolved, and as a verb it means to sink below the horizon.

clue.text: Conventional phrases I used in features

indicators.note: used in means put inside, so the letter goes within

parts.note: noses are facial features

explanation.surface: Someone describes using stock expressions in facial characteristics.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside NOSES. To 'make the right noises' is to say the expected conventional things.
explanation.definitionFit: Making the right noises means uttering conventional, expected remarks without real commitment.

clue.text: Church officer attacked violently when carrying cross

indicators.note: carrying means holding within, so the cross is inside

parts.note: to be set on is to be attacked
X is shaped like a cross

explanation.surface: A church official was assaulted while carrying a crucifix.
explanation.walkthrough: X goes inside SET ON, after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: A sexton is a church officer who looks after the building and churchyard.

clue.text: Clever boy presented with storybooks

indicators.note: presented with places the boy alongside the storybooks

parts.note: a tale is a story
NT is the New Testament, a collection of books
Ed is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A clever boy is given some storybooks.
explanation.walkthrough: One word, 'storybooks', is split into two halves, each supplying its own synonym; the books are the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Talented means gifted, having natural ability, a near synonym of clever.
